plain_summary: Review lamotrigine exposure when an oestrogen-containing combined oral contraceptive is started, used or stopped.

medicine_groups.name: Oestrogen-containing combined oral contraceptives
medicine_groups.note: Count both ingredients in the same oral contraceptive, in either order. Exclude vaginal rings, patches, hormone replacement therapy and progestogen-only products.

rule_for_models: Cite both supplies and any recorded start or stop when an oestrogen-containing combined oral pill starts, overlaps or has a documented stop (including a switch) during lamotrigine treatment, whatever the reason for either medicine. Compare treatment dates using supply dates, pack counts, tablets per pack and the recorded regimen including placebo or planned tablet-free days, without treating a scheduled break or missed refill alone as a stop. If the regimen or dates are unclear and the supplies could overlap, report a possible finding and ask when the pill was started or stopped, how it was taken and whether symptom control or side effects changed.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish actual use, indication or a prescriber’s intent. Treatment and assessments elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the lamotrigine dose, symptom control and possible side effects in light of when the patient started, took or stopped the combined pill?
